init.title: Control D settings
init.description: What would you like to configure?

data_description.managed_in_home_assistant: Turn off to exclude this profile and remove its entities from Home Assistant.
data_description.expose_external_filters: Create disabled-by-default entities for available 3rd-party filters while still keeping them available to services either way.
data_description.advanced_profile_options: Create the remaining profile option entities for this profile in disabled-by-default state.
data_description.expose_all_active_services: Turn on to expose the current explicit profile service rows. This cannot be combined with specific service category selections. Leave off to expose only the selected service categories below, or no service entities if no categories are selected.
data_description.endpoint_sensors_enabled: Create telemetry entities for devices under this profile.
data_description.endpoint_inactivity_threshold_minutes: How long before an endpoint is marked as inactive.
data_description.allowed_service_categories: Select one or more categories to expose only those services. This cannot be combined with Expose all active services. Category-created entities are disabled by default.
data_description.expose_all_custom_rules: Turn on to expose every current folder and custom rule for this profile. This cannot be combined with specific custom rule selections. Leave off to expose only the selected custom rules below, or no custom rule entities if none are selected.
data_description.exposed_custom_rules: Select specific custom rule folders or domains to expose as switches. This cannot be combined with Expose all custom rules.

data_description.configuration_sync_interval_minutes: How often to fetch the currently implemented Control D inventory and configuration data, including profiles, endpoints, filters, options, default rules, and any enabled service or rule catalogs. Default: 15.
data_description.llm_tool_mode: How much of the integration an AI assistant or MCP client may reach. This is independent of the entity exposure settings above. Off registers nothing; Summary only sends account counts and each profile's name with its counts; Read only adds endpoint and client names, addresses, and query-level analytics; Read and control adds reversible changes; Full adds destructive actions. Changing anything through these tools also requires an administrator: a non-admin user is rejected by the services themselves. Requires Home Assistant 2026.10 or newer.

delete_client.name: Delete client
delete_client.description: DESTRUCTIVE and irreversible. Delete client rows from one or more Control D endpoints, resolved from client ID, MAC address, endpoint name, hostname, or IP address within one selected config entry. Client IDs take precedence over the other selectors. The client row is derived from observed traffic, so an ordinary client reappears the next time it is seen; a client that will not recur, such as one using a rotating private MAC, stays deleted. Stored query history for these clients is purged as well unless delete_history is false.

client_id.name: Client IDs
client_id.description: Required unless you provide Endpoint MAC addresses, Endpoint names, Endpoint hostnames, or Endpoint IP addresses. Enter one or more Control D client IDs, separated by commas, such as 04070f91bf7d,d18cc9582f25. If multiple selector families are provided, Client IDs take precedence. This is the only selector that always matches a single client.

endpoint_mac.name: Endpoint MAC addresses
endpoint_mac.description: Required unless you provide Client IDs, Endpoint names, Endpoint hostnames, or Endpoint IP addresses. Enter one or more client MAC addresses, separated by commas, such as 50:eb:71:b6:78:3a,3c:52:a1:11:22:33. Several clients under one endpoint can share a MAC, so a MAC may match more than one client and more will be deleted than intended.

endpoint_name.name: Endpoint names
endpoint_name.description: Required unless you provide Client IDs, Endpoint MAC addresses, Endpoint hostnames, or Endpoint IP addresses. Enter one or more Control D endpoint names, separated by commas, such as Chads-Phone,Kitchen Tablet.

endpoint_hostname.name: Endpoint hostnames
endpoint_hostname.description: Required unless you provide Client IDs, Endpoint MAC addresses, Endpoint names, or Endpoint IP addresses. Enter one or more analytics hostnames, separated by commas. A rotating private MAC produces many rows under one hostname, so a hostname such as watch can match a long list of clients.

endpoint_ip.name: Endpoint IP addresses
endpoint_ip.description: Required unless you provide Client IDs, Endpoint MAC addresses, Endpoint names, or Endpoint hostnames. Enter one or more client IP addresses, separated by commas.

parent_endpoint_name.name: Parent endpoint name
parent_endpoint_name.description: Optional. Narrow ambiguous hostname, name, or IP matches to one parent endpoint such as Firewalla-VLAN60.

delete_history.name: Delete query history
delete_history.description: Optional, defaults to true. When true, the stored DNS query history for the deleted clients is purged as well. Set to false to remove only the client rows and keep their history.

set_rule_state.description: Enable or disable one or more Control D custom rules by stable identity across the selected profiles, and optionally change their action mode, redirect target, comment, or expiration. Redirect targets are only applied when Mode is redirect. If Cancel expiration is set, it overrides Expiration duration and Expire at. Otherwise, Expire at takes precedence over Expiration duration.

rule_identity.name: Rule identities
rule_identity.description: Required. Enter one or more stable Control D rule identities, such as root|example.com or group:1|example2.com. You can also use a bare hostname such as example.com when it is unambiguous.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Optional. Turn the selected rules on or off for the targeted profiles. If omitted, the current enabled state is preserved.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Optional. Change the selected rules to block, bypass, or redirect. If omitted, the current rule action is preserved.

redirect_target.name: Redirect target
redirect_target.description: Optional. Redirect destination. Use a Control D location code or name, LOCAL for auto routing, ? for random routing, or an IP address for proxy redirects.

redirect_target_type.name: Redirect target type
redirect_target_type.description: Optional. Redirect target family. When omitted, the integration infers ipv4 or ipv6 from a valid IP address and treats other values, including LOCAL and ?, as location-family redirects.

comment.name: Comment
comment.description: Optional. Replace the selected rule comment. Provide an empty string to clear it.

cancel_expiration.name: Cancel expiration
cancel_expiration.description: Optional. Cancel the current rule expiration. When set, this overrides Expiration duration and Expire at.

expiration_duration.name: Expiration duration
expiration_duration.description: Optional. Set the selected rules to expire after a relative duration such as 30 minutes. Ignored when Cancel expiration is set or when Expire at is also provided.

expire_at.name: Expire at
expire_at.description: Optional. Set the selected rules to expire at an absolute date and time in the Home Assistant local timezone. Ignored when Cancel expiration is set. When both Expiration duration and Expire at are provided, this field takes precedence. Past values are allowed.

set_endpoint_profile.name: Set endpoint profile
set_endpoint_profile.description: Attach the profile an endpoint enforces, and optionally a second one, resolved by endpoint ID within one selected config entry. An endpoint always enforces one profile, so the primary can be changed but not emptied; the secondary is optional and can be cleared with clear_profile2. When two profiles are enforced, the rule engine merges them before matching rather than applying them in order.

endpoint_id.name: Endpoint IDs
endpoint_id.description: Required. Enter one or more Control D endpoint device IDs, separated by commas, such as 461wtt4eyr,w1eg4mfif8. IDs are unique, so this is the safe selector.

profile_id.name: Primary profile
profile_id.description: Optional. The profile PK to enforce as the primary, such as 962691chipwa5. A profile name is also accepted. Omit to leave the primary unchanged.

profile2_id.name: Secondary profile
profile2_id.description: Optional. The profile PK to enforce as the secondary, such as 886818chik7jg. Omit to leave the secondary unchanged.

clear_profile2.name: Clear secondary profile
clear_profile2.description: Optional, defaults to false. Set true to detach the secondary profile, leaving only the primary. The primary cannot be cleared, because an endpoint always enforces one profile.

create_endpoint.name: Create endpoint
create_endpoint.description: Create one Control D endpoint, which is a DNS resolver that enforces a profile, within one selected config entry. A profile is required because an endpoint always enforces exactly one and the platform has no endpoint without one. The name must be unique across the account. Optionally set a description, an icon slug, and the initial analytics logging level.

endpoint_name.name: Endpoint name
endpoint_name.description: Required. The display name for the new endpoint. Must be unique across the account; a duplicate is rejected.

profile_id.name: Profile
profile_id.description: Required. The profile PK the new endpoint enforces, such as 962691chipwa5. A profile name is also accepted. An endpoint always enforces exactly one profile, so this cannot be omitted.

description.name: Description
description.description: Optional. A free-text note stored on the endpoint.

icon.name: Icon
icon.description: Optional. An icon slug, for example desktop-linux or router.

mode.name: Analytics logging level
mode.description: Optional. The initial analytics logging level: None, Some (block/redirect/bypass counts only), or Full (also records the queries themselves). Logging stays off when omitted.

config_entry_id.description: Optional. Only needed when more than one Control D integration is loaded. If both Configuration Entry ID and Configuration Entry name are provided, Configuration Entry ID takes precedence.

delete_endpoint.name: Delete endpoint
delete_endpoint.description: DESTRUCTIVE and irreversible. Delete one or more Control D endpoints resolved by endpoint ID or display name within one selected config entry. Endpoint IDs take precedence over names. Deleting an endpoint removes the resolver itself and the records kept against it, so whatever resolved through it stops being filtered; deleting a router endpoint affects every device behind it.

endpoint_id.name: Endpoint IDs
endpoint_id.description: Optional. Enter one or more Control D endpoint device IDs, separated by commas, such as 461wtt4eyr,w1eg4mfif8. IDs are unique, so this is the safer selector. If both Endpoint IDs and Endpoint names are provided, Endpoint IDs take precedence.

endpoint_name.name: Endpoint names
endpoint_name.description: Optional. Enter one or more Control D endpoint names, separated by commas, such as Chads-Phone,Kitchen Tablet. Endpoint names are not guaranteed to be unique, so prefer the endpoint ID.

set_endpoint_description.description: Set the free-text note an endpoint carries, resolved by endpoint ID or display name within one selected config entry. Endpoint IDs take precedence over names. An empty string clears the description, because the API drops the field rather than keeping a blank value. This changes no behaviour.
